newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian buyers start '97 Murban crude term talks.
newsitem.headline: Asian buyers start '97 Murban crude term talks.

text.p: Negotiations between Abu Dhabi crude equity holders and some Asian customers on 1997 term contracts have started, traders said on Thursday.
Equity holders are expected to aim for a premium of about 30 cents above ADNOC for Murban crude, while buyers are seen aiming for about 25 cents, traders said.
In the past year, the premium of the Middle Eastern crude has averaged about 27 cents in the spot market, traders said.
Under 1996 term contracts, Murban was priced at a premium of about 22 cents to ADNOC, down two cents from the 1995 price of 24 cents.
The average spot premium is used as a guideline to decide the term premium.
Murban has enjoyed high premiums this year, partly because of good demand from Japanese refiners who needed to replenish their kerosene stockpiles.
Light crudes tend to yield a greater amount of kerosene compared to heavy grades.
